task.title: Build 63 Founder acceptance diagnosis — 2 fixes prepared, 1 cleared with no code change

result.summary: Diagnosed all three FAILED Build 63 Founder acceptance items with production evidence rather than assumption. Item 2 (Your Journey progress bars): root-caused to ActiveGoalCurrentStateSections.journey -- the actual render path for any goal with server-populated currentState, e.g. the Founder's real 'Build Lean Mass' -- calling GoalPhaseCard with showsProgress:false based on a stale, disproven comment; the existing regression test used a Sandbox fixture lacking currentState so it silently tested the wrong code path. Fixed with a one-line change plus a new RED/GREEN test against the fixture that does have currentState. Item 3 (Completed Visible Abs photos): a zero-write production DB read, reproducing the exact server pipeline (composeCompletedGoalPreview, resolveCompletedGoalPhoto, resolveProgressPhotoMedia, resolveBriefingMedia/resolveNarrativeMedia) line for line, proves both Beginning and Completion photos already resolve to valid /media/<id> hrefs pointing at verified, fully-populated media objects -- no code defect found on either side, so per the explicit 'do not invent new semantics' instruction, nothing was changed; recommending the Founder simply re-check the screen. Item 4 (Strength reconciliation -999): ruled out every app-owned cancellation mechanism findable by code review (no custom URLSession, no explicit cancel, no task racing anywhere in the app) while a zero-write command_receipts read confirms this exact command type has never once landed server-side across two prior independently-shipped fix attempts, while every other command type flows normally in the same windows. Could not fully prove app-owned vs external causation, so per instruction added a diagnostic-only Task.isCancelled capture at the exact catch site instead of a guessed behavioral fix.

tests.summary: Full PhysiqueOSTests target: 1446/1446 passing (1445 prior + 1 new). Both new RED/GREEN tests (testCurrentStateJourneyPhaseCardsShowProgressMatchingHomeSinceNoOtherSectionDoes, testPreservesTaskCancellationStateAtCatch) independently confirmed RED before their respective fixes and GREEN after. UI tests: GoalsAcceptanceUITests 1/1, TrainingAcceptanceUITests 12/12 -- no regression to Logged Today Cardio or any other previously-accepted behavior.

review.summary: Independent fresh-context review (zero prior context) verified the diff directly against the code: confirmed both GoalPhaseCard call sites and that Journey is the only section on the current-state page that can show per-phase progress; confirmed the Task.isCancelled capture runs before the catch block's only await with no control-flow change and no hidden suspension point; confirmed both new tests build and pass; confirmed git diff --stat touches exactly the 6 described files with no build-number or unrelated change. No issues found.

release_build.summary: Not run this pass -- free disk space was at/under the 15 GiB STANDING_DISK_SAFETY.md hard floor after clearing the already-uploaded Build 63 archive, and a Release build was judged too disk-risky to force through. Debug build-for-testing succeeded cleanly and the full unit+UI suites above ran against it.

zero_write_audit.summary: Two separate zero-write, owner-scoped, ROLLBACK-guaranteed production DB audits (physiqueos.canonical_evidence_records/canonical_briefing_records/canonical_media_objects for the Visible Abs photo pipeline; physiqueos.command_receipts for the Strength reconciliation receipt check), both verified transaction_read_only=on before reading, both rolled back cleanly.

unexpected_findings: The prior session's Visible Abs photo diagnosis direction (a stale/unresolved briefing href) was disproven on a second, more careful trace: the briefing narrative's raw legacy href IS correctly re-resolved by resolveBriefingMedia/resolveNarrativeMedia before composeCompletedGoalPreview ever sees it. Both photos' server-side data is fully valid right now -- worth remembering as a caution about verifying a fix hypothesis against the FULL real pipeline (including steps that happen upstream of the function you're staring at), not just the function itself.
